rules.statement: A vendor is bound to make full and free delivery of the property sold, including putting the purchaser in actual possession. Where a sale deed contains an express covenant for freedom from encumbrances, and the encumbrance makes it impossible for the vendor to give vacant possession, the sale can be rescinded.
rules.supporting_quote: "It is true that according to some of the Dutch writers., (Van Leeuwen 4, 19, 5; Voet 19, 1, 6) a purchaser is not entitled to cancel the sale when land has been sold without any mention of a servitude or other encumbrance upon it, and such a servitude or encumbrance is in fact found to exist, but this view of the law has not been accepted by the Courts in British Guiana (see 21 , 8. A. L. 1), and it does not seem to me that these expressions of opinion can be intended to conflict with the clear law that full and free possession must be given"
